Abstract

Background
The accurate delineation of glioma boundaries from magnetic resonance imaging remains challenging due to irregular tumor margins and heterogeneous intensity patterns.

Methods
We propose an adaptive superpixel graph-cut framework that first constructs boundary-aware superpixels using a parameter-free clustering strategy, then extracts statistical, texture, and curvature descriptors for each region, and finally applies a support vector machine for refined classification.

Results
Experiments on a benchmark brain tumor dataset demonstrate stable segmentation performance across tumor grades, with improved overlap and boundary adherence compared with standard superpixel baselines.

Conclusions
The method provides a reproducible and efficient approach for automatic glioma segmentation and supports clinical pre-screening workflows.

result.title: Adaptive Superpixel Graph Cuts for Glioma Boundary Delineation
